rationale: Single module-boundary replacement of the whole observed stem bundle at model.resnet.embedder (ResNetEmbeddings, call fa7ef6548e3a2d54174caeba). The frozen objective is peak_allocated_bytes for one offline batch-32 FP32 forward (baseline 281,975,808 B) with images_per_second >= 0.95 of baseline. The measured peak is set by the eager stem: during aten::batch_norm the conv1 output (32x64x112x112 fp32 = 102,760,448 B) and the BN output (another 102,760,448 B) are simultaneously live on top of resident weights (11,689,512 params = 46,758,048 B) and the GPU-resident pixels (19,267,584 B), with the maxpool 3x3 s2 int64 index buffer (51.38 MB at batch 32) and conv workspace making up the remainder. conv2d, eval-mode batch_norm (frozen running stats, training=False), relu and max_pool2d are all strictly per-sample operators, so the replacement streams the batch through the identical parent operators in fixed 8-sample chunks (4 chunks for the frozen batch 32; the remainder loop handles any other batch without changing the frozen workload) and copies each pooled chunk into one preallocated (32,64,56,56) output tensor returned to stage 0. No operator, dtype, batch, sequence, sampling, precision policy, TF32/cudnn setting, quality threshold or completion boundary changes: every chunk still executes the observed parent aten operators aten.conv2d (8504783bbca736066fecb204), aten.batch_norm (89bc7485bcb9aeaa62c7d28b), aten.relu (89f968d79a78e013c08bd56c) and aten.max_pool2d (4367176c34e4141fee648ee6) through context['references'], so the parent work executes on every invocation (4 reference invocations per site per forward, recorded in path telemetry), and no functional replacements are installed, so no dispatch-mode overhead or interception is added on any other operator in the project. Predicted warm-run peak: during a chunk only conv_out + bn_out (2 x 25.69 MB) plus the retained 25.69 MB output are live, so the stem moment drops from ~271.5 MB of live tensors to ~143 MB + small per-chunk conv workspace and 12.84 MB chunk index buffers; after the stem fix the invocation peak moves to the unchanged stage-0 residual moment (~46.76 weights + 19.27 pixels + 4 x 25.69 MB live activations ~ 168.8 MB), which is the honest floor for a stem-only edit per the selection analysis. Expected peak_allocated_bytes ~169-176 MB versus 281.98 MB (~38-40% lower), with the exact value to be measured by the paired evaluator. Latency: total stem bytes moved are unchanged for conv/BN/ReLU (same aggregate sizes), the only added traffic is 4 contiguous device-to-device copies of 6.42 MB each (~51 MB total) plus ~15 extra host launches, which the observed ~2 ms host dispatch slack and 224.7 us latency budget (floor 4.4942 ms vs 4.2695 ms baseline) absorb; GPU kernels remain the same bandwidth-bound families at the same aggregate sizes. No previous feedback exists (inputs/previous-feedback.txt absent and no inputs/previous-candidate), so this is the first attempt at the selected region; BN-folding into conv1 was deliberately not used because the stage-0 moment already bounds the peak after chunking, so folding would add rounding-reordering risk with no additional memory benefit; an in-place ReLU was likewise not used because the parent out-of-place aten.relu site is available through its reference and the stem moment is already below the stage-0 floor. Fallback discipline: build resolves the parent reference, the three physical modules (Conv2d a929588cc0791799075542c6, BatchNorm2d d2690ee924ab33cd95efa6f0, MaxPool2d 12da68be9b9e14502fe4702a) and the four operator references; if resolution fails the returned callable routes every call to the parent under the 'setup_failure_parent' route label; signature/attribute guards (CUDA fp32 4-D input matching in_channels, eval-mode affine track-stats BN, zeros padding, groups=1, no indices/ceil_mode pooling) route unsupported calls to the parent under 'unsupported_signature_parent'; a mid-computation operator exception routes to the parent under 'runtime_failure_parent'. The chosen chunked path self-reports 'chunked_stem_composite' via context['record_route'] invoked inside the replacement.
setup_work: build(context) performs no GPU work and allocates no device memory: it only resolves the observed modules and parent/operator references into Python closures and reads nothing from the fixture. No model parameters are transformed, packed or copied, no CUDA Graph is captured, no global torch backend/math flag is touched (evaluator's math_policy check stays green), and nothing is cached across invocations: every call recomputes the stem from its live input. Per-chunk temporaries (25.69 MB conv/BN/ReLU outputs, 6.42 MB pooled chunk, 12.84 MB int64 pool indices) and the single 25.69 MB output tensor are allocated inside each invocation through the caching allocator, so after the warmup invocations they are served from cached blocks; the setup receipt's allocated_bytes after installation remains the prepared model + pixels exactly as the parent. Retained allocator pools may come to include the 25.69/12.84 MB block classes used by the chunked path (framework.reserved/lifecycle counters can differ from the parent), while the objective framework.peak_allocated_bytes is reset per invocation and reflects only live allocations; the predicted decrease is specific to the warm-run peak_allocated_bytes counter of this workload, not a general physical-memory saving.
quality_risks: Chunked conv2d runs cudnn's heuristic at batch 8 instead of batch 32 (cudnn.benchmark stays False). For this 3->64 7x7 stride-2 convolution the implicit-GEMM family accumulates each output element over the same 147-element reduction independently of the batch dimension, so per-sample results are expected to be bitwise identical (verified bitwise-exact for the per-sample operators in CPU plumbing tests); if a different algorithm were selected, per-element differences are fp32 round-off (~1e-6 relative), far below the frozen logits tolerance atol=rtol=1e-4 and immaterial to argmax margins, but this is the one numerics uncertainty and is left to the frozen evaluator's closeness, exact-top1 and +1-corruption checks.

Latency floor risk: ~15 extra host launches (hidden by the observed ~2 ms host slack) and ~51 MB of extra D2D copy traffic (~60-170 us depending on achieved copy bandwidth) against the 224.7 us budget; if a chunked cudnn algorithm were slower the chunk size is retunable inside the same boundary without changing the frozen semantics.

The four aten sites now execute with chunk-shaped signatures through context['references']; on the next discovery recapture they will be re-keyed under new call ids with the chunk signature (the framework recaptures the plan; consumers of the stem output still receive a contiguous (32,64,56,56) fp32 CUDA tensor exactly as the parent pooler produced).

Fallback labels keep the failure taxonomy observable: 'setup_failure_parent' (unresolved modules/references), 'unsupported_signature_parent' (guard mismatch, e.g. training mode, non-fp32/CPU tensors, non-zeros padding, grouped conv, indices/ceil_mode pooling), 'runtime_failure_parent' (operator exception mid-composite, full parent recompute). The framework's signature guard additionally only dispatches the observed (32,3,224,224) call to the replacement at all.
eliminated_calls_rationale: The whole stem bundle inside model.resnet.embedder is replaced at its boundary, so the inner Python module calls no longer execute as module calls: ResNetConvLayer (fad32b28bd6e0def6ce7593e), Conv2d (a929588cc0791799075542c6), BatchNorm2d (d2690ee924ab33cd95efa6f0), ReLU (9bb381a7b50f1e3dcfdb1cb4) and MaxPool2d (12da68be9b9e14502fe4702a). Their computational content is preserved exactly: the replacement reads the same live module parameters (conv weight/stride/padding, BN affine and running stats, pool geometry) and executes the equivalent aten operators through context['references'] on every invocation; only the intermediate Python module boundaries and the full-resolution temporaries they materialized are gone. The only consumer of these calls' outputs is the stem itself, which returns the same contiguous (32,64,56,56) fp32 CUDA tensor to the encoder stages, so all downstream consumers remain valid. The profiler record_function enter/exit sites (1f750cfe73af31647514bce9, 5a738567860d1790e17b4c74, 74a7d1dc7c252585bac9ee72, 9beb8b9076cc061fb8023ead, 9d3d81c3c57605e001aa0979, a263d10c24fce1ff47e60d76, b04ed2ee2118d432096eebe4) are discovery instrumentation markers around the captured ops, not computational work; their consumers are trace analysis only, and the framework's recapture will emit fresh markers for the chunked path.
